title: A poor lookout for Corny
html_source:
A second instance in this chapter where Bloom favors modernization.

Bloom first wondered why someone couldn’t invent an automatic railway switch. It might put pointsmen out of work but “another fellow would get a job making the new invention.”

Now, Bloom envisions a livestock train and a funeral tram, rather than cattle droving and horse-drawn funeral carriages.

When Mr Power observes that a funeral tram would cut into Corny Kelleher’s undertaking business, Bloom thinks modernization is the better course. He seems to convince the other men in the carriage.

Beyond the characterization of Bloom as a forward-thinking person, there might be a slight hint here of old things passing away in this chapter that so often addresses death.
